steps.title: Add water gradually
steps.text: Begin with approximately 70–80 ml lukewarm water per 100 g flour and adjust as needed.

steps.title: Rest

steps.title: Add warm water gradually
steps.text: Begin with approximately 75–90 ml water per 100 g flour and adjust carefully.

steps.title: Mix gently
steps.text: Combine thoroughly until the flour is evenly hydrated. Gluten-free dough does not require wheat-style gluten development.

steps.title: Rest

steps.title: Shape gently

steps.title: Cook & serve
steps.text: Cook on a preheated tawa. Avoid prolonged cooking and keep covered after cooking.

steps.title: Add water gradually
steps.text: Start with approximately 60–70 ml water per 100 g flour. Increase gradually as required.

steps.title: Knead well
steps.text: Knead for around 4–6 minutes until the dough becomes smooth and workable.

steps.title: Rest
steps.text: Cover and rest for approximately 15–20 minutes to allow the flour to hydrate.

steps.title: Roll evenly
steps.text: Use moderate pressure and avoid using excessive dry flour.

steps.title: Cook on a hot tawa
steps.text: Cook both sides properly and avoid prolonged cooking to help retain softness.

steps.title: Keep covered
steps.text: Place cooked rotis in a covered container or cloth.

littleFacts.question: Does it taste sweet?
littleFacts.answer: It may have a mild natural sweetness, but it is not a sweetened product.

littleFacts.question: Is it gluten-free?
littleFacts.answer: No. Sharbati is a wheat variety and contains gluten.

littleFacts.question: What is it suitable for?
